title: NeedleFinder: Enterprise Ask Aggregation & Rapid Scope Canvas
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Summary: NeedleFinder is a lightweight aggregation and rapid scoping playbook + artifact set for high-volume Sales/CS enterprise feature asks (non-bug). The goal is to convert noisy inbound requests into triaged, scored, and minimally scoped micro-PRDs that allow PM/Eng/Design to make fast go/no-go and sizing decisions. This effort targets the top-of-funnel for enterprise intake: collection normalization, account-aware prioritization, econ-impact signals, and an auto-populated one-page scope canvas that can be handed to Solutions Engineering or used for discovery sprints.

Why now: Sales and CS volume has increased with Dedicated and Private conversations. We need a predictable, repeatable front door that turns requests into decision-ready artifacts without heavy manual PM time. This reduces time-to-first-response, improves prioritization fidelity, and feeds our product backlog with better-quality asks.

Scope:
- Input normalization templates (email/CS ticket/GSheet to canonical fields).
- Account-weighted scoring rubric (ARR, product footprint, strategic tier, regulatory requirement, implementation complexity).
- Rapid Scope Canvas: a one-page micro-PRD capturing problem statement, success metrics, 1-sentence technical approach, rough effort (T-shirt), customer risk, and rollout path (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Aggregator dashboard mock: sortable queue for Product/SE with quick filters and auto-suggested owners.
- 10 sample scoped briefs from recent inbound requests to validate rubric.

Out-of-scope (for this ticket): full engineering spec, legal/compliance sign-off flows, detailed resource allocation for Delivered projects.

Acceptance criteria:
- Documented scoring rubric with example scoring applied to 10 historical requests.
- Rapid Scope Canvas template in Confluence and a Fillable Google Form for Sales/CS.
- Aggregator dashboard prototype (Figma mock + a single dashboard query in Looker/Metabase for early validation).
- Playbook doc outlining handoff rules and SLA for first response (<= 3 business days) and when to escalate to Solutions Eng.
- Stakeholder sign-off from Sales/CS lead and two Eng reps.

Interfaces and integrations:
- Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/NeedleFinder+Playbook (placeholder)
- Fillable intake form (Drive): https://drive.google.com/NeedleFinderIntake (placeholder)
- Example GH links to followups will be attached after scoping.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Low adoption by Sales if process is heavy. Mitigation: 2-click Triage + pre-filled fields from CRM export; create Slack shortcut for intake.
- Risk: Over-scoping by PMs. Mitigation: enforce 3-point rubric (impact, effort, strategic fit) and timebox discovery to 2 weeks for medium-high cases.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 0-2: Draft rubric, rapid canvas, and 10-sample retrospective scoring.
- Week 3-4: Figma dashboard prototype + Fillable intake form; pilot with 3 AE/CS teams.
- Week 5-6: Iterate with pilot feedback, produce handoff playbook and acceptance criteria.

Stakeholders: Sales/CS (Bridget Kim), Solutions Eng (Diego Ramos), Design (Priya Narang), Eng leads (Ethan Green, Jun Park).
comments: 2025-11-19 — Kickoff: met with Bridget (Sales) and Diego (SE). Agreed scope focused on non-bug feature asks and regulatory requests. Sales requested ability to mark requests as ‘time-sensitive’ and provide customer ROI expectations.

2025-11-26 — Draft scoring rubric shared. Initial signals: ARR band, product footprint (Embeddings / API usage / Dedicated), regulatory flag (yes/no), implementation complexity (S/M/L). Diego suggested adding 'migration cost' dimension for Dedicated->Private transitions.

2025-12-04 — Design sync (Priya): produced first Rapid Scope Canvas prototype in Figma. Canvas limited to single page to improve scanability. Feedback: reduce free-text fields; use picklists derived from rubric.

2026-01-12 — Engineering review: Ethan and Jun reviewed and requested a mandatory 'compatibility' field mapping to product surfaces (hosted / dedicated / private) and a note for data residency constraints. Also requested sample acceptance tests for each brief.
2026-02-02 — Pilot plan: pilot with three AE teams for 3 weeks. Will instrument a Google Form intake and auto-populate a GSheet that feeds the dashboard. Morgan to own the pilot orchestration.

2026-02-15 — Early pilot feedback: intake adoption at ~60% for flagged enterprise leads; Sales requested pre-population via CRM export — added as follow-up task. Some ambiguity in 'implementation complexity' led to variance in scoring; engineering will provide a quick-check matrix to reduce variance.

2026-03-02 — PM review: updated rubric with weighted scoring (Impact 40%, Strategic Fit 30%, Effort -20%, Compliance 10%). Created mapping rules to derive a triage status: Quick Win / Discovery / Requires Proposal / No-Fit.

2026-03-10 — Ready for stakeholder sign-off. Meetings scheduled next week with Bridget and Diego. Next: ship Confluence playbook, Figma dashboard link, and 10 sample scoped briefs. Action: Morgan to prepare pilot retrospective and rollout checklist.
